title: Realization of an integral lattice stratum by a proper tame pair
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Put $A_{E,T}=p_T^*C(-,E)$ and $A_{\mathcal O_E,T}=p_T^*C(-,\mathcal O_E)$, with continuous-map condensed rings and their norm topologies [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $\Dbc(T,A_E)$ for bounded complexes with finite constant local models on finite constructible stratifications [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free, including rank zero [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion and $a:S\hookrightarrow U$ a nonempty integral locally closed subscheme. Let $T$ be the reduced closure of $S$ in $X$, put $T^\circ=T\cap U$, and assume $S$ is dense open in $T^\circ$. Let $M_0$ be a lisse finite-rank $A_{\mathcal O_E,S}$-module and put $M=M_0[1/\ell]$.

There exist a regular integral $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], a proper dominant generically finite map $h:Y\to T$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], a finite reduced strict normal crossings divisor $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] and $A_{\rm out}\subseteq A$ such that
$$W=h^{-1}S=Y\setminus D,\qquad V=h^{-1}T^\circ=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\in A_{\rm out}}D_a.$$
Write $p:Y\to T\hookrightarrow X$, $q:V\to U$, $r:W\to S$, and $b:W\hookrightarrow V$ for the induced maps. Then $p,q,r$ are proper, $V=p^{-1}U$, and $L=r^*M$ is lisse and tame along $D$: at every geometric point of $Y$, for every choice of strict-local regular parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ for $D$, its pullback to the inverse-limit cover of the punctured strict henselization obtained by adjoining compatible $n$th roots of these parameters for all $(n,p)=1$ is constant [def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module]. The case $s=0$ uses the identity cover.

There is a nonempty dense open $v:S_0\hookrightarrow S$ such that $r_0:W_0=W\times_S S_0\to S_0$ factors as a finite universal homeomorphism $u:W_0\to T_0$ followed by a finite etale surjection $e:T_0\to S_0$ of constant degree $d\geq1$ [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. No separability of $k(Y)/k(T)$ is required. Set
$$N=Rr_*(L[0]),\qquad G=Rq_*((b_!L)[0]),$$
using exact open extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Then $b_!L$ is constructible, $N\in\Dbc(S,A_E)$, $G\in\Dbc(U,A_E)$, and there are canonical derived isomorphisms
$$G\simeq a_!N,\qquad v^*N\simeq Rr_{0*}(r_0^*(M|_{S_0})[0]).$$
Here $a_!$ has the normalized locally closed meaning [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]. In particular $G$ is zero outside the closure of $S$ in $U$. Empty boundaries and empty outer subsets are allowed. No SNC condition for $Y\setminus W_0$ is asserted, and no thick-generation conclusion is included.

source.place: Agent assembly from X Theorem 2.1, printed pp.149-151, and the existing nested-open alteration and potential Kummer-tameness inputs; proper/open interchange through det-sf-comp-composition-interchange(3), motivated by Stacks 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), not its torsion-only direct application; original item steps 4,5,7.

proof.text: Use lem-sfb-normed-coefficient-realization to identify the normed coefficient pair $(\mathcal O_E,E)$ isometrically with an embedded finite-extension pair. We may work with this pair and transport back at the end: the cited equivalences commute with actual derived direct images and preserve bounds. They also preserve finite constant models, since applying the scalar isomorphism to a presentation over $E$ gives the corresponding presentation over the isomorphic field. Finite free local models and the property of being constant after a given pullback are preserved in the same way. Inverse images and open extension by zero are transported by relabelling the ring action on the same underlying abelian sheaves; hence their units and the comparisons below transport as well. This introduces neither a larger coefficient field nor a new coefficient topology. All schemes used below are Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, applied over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Section 6.8, finite coefficient fields; coefficient-isomorphism transport made explicit by the cited realization node.

proof.text: The reduced closure $T$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by def-pc-integral-scheme. Indeed a closure of an irreducible subset is irreducible: two proper closed subsets covering the closure would restrict to two proper closed subsets covering its dense irreducible subset. Thus $S$ is connected. Apply lem-sfb-lisse-lattice-potential-kummer-tameness to $M_0$ to choose a connected finite etale surjection $c:H\to S$ with its stated universal parameter-root property. Apply lem-sfb-nested-open-regular-alteration to $S\subseteq T^\circ\subseteq T$ and this particular cover. Its hypotheses hold: the two opens are dense since $S$ is dense in $T$, and $S$ is open in $T$ because it is open in the open $T^\circ$. Obtain $Y,h,D,A_{\rm out},W,V,r$ and a factorization $W\to H\to S$. The same node supplies the nonempty dense open $S_0$ and the finite universal-homeomorphism/finite-etale factorization of $r_0$, including constant degree $d\geq1$. Keep the original boundary $D$ when making this generic restriction.

source.place: X Theorem 2.1, printed p.149, through the nested-open alteration input; IX Proposition 2.1, printed pp.133-134, and Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 6.8.4 through the potential-tameness input.

proof.text: Let $s:S\hookrightarrow T^\circ$ and $i:T^\circ\hookrightarrow U$ be the open and closed immersions, so $a=is$. The base change $h_V:V\to T^\circ$ of $h$ and its further base change $r:W\to S$ are proper by lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change. The closed immersions $T\hookrightarrow X$ and $i$ are proper by lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper; composition with $h$ and $h_V$ gives proper $p$ and $q$ by lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition. The inverse-image identity $V=p^{-1}U$ follows from $T^\circ=T\cap U$. The coefficient pullback is exact and identifies pulled-back rings by sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients. Consequently pulling a finite free local presentation of $M=M_0[1/\ell]$ back to $W$ gives a finite free local presentation of $L=r^*M$. Here scalar inversion is extension to $A_E$; locally the presentation $A_{\mathcal O_E}^n$ becomes $A_E^n$. Since $r$ factors through the chosen $H$, the universal property in lem-sfb-lisse-lattice-potential-kummer-tameness gives exactly the asserted constancy on every strict-local parameter-root tower, for every choice of parameters, including the identity tower when no parameter occurs.

source.place: X Theorem 2.1 and IX Proposition 2.1 as assembled in the two cited inputs; properness is the base-change/composition calculus of the cited nodes.

proof.text: On a pro-etale cover trivializing $L$, its local model is $A_E\otimes_E E^n$, with $E^n$ finitely presented, so $L$ is constructible in the precise finite constant-model sense of sk-def-sfb-constructible. Moreover tensoring with $A_E^n$ is the finite direct-sum functor, which is exact. This is checked after a covering, where kernels and cokernels of sheaf maps restrict to the corresponding kernels and cokernels; hence $L$ is flat and $L[0]$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. Its cohomology is also concentrated in $[0,0]$. Apply lem-sfb-open-extension-zero-constructible-finite-tor to $b:W\hookrightarrow V$: it gives that $b_!L$ is finite constant-model constructible, $(b_!L)[0]\in\Dctf(V,A_E)$, and bounded constructibility in the stratified locally finitely presented sense as well. Thus the two notions required in the next step both hold for the degree-zero inputs, without identifying these notions for arbitrary modules.

source.place: Clause (3), finite-Tor input for proper/open interchange; finite free tensor calculation and the stated open-extension preservation theorem.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-proper-dc-preserves-continuous to the proper maps $r$ and $q$, with degree-zero inputs $L$ and $b_!L$. Their bases are Noetherian by step 1; their coefficient ring is the actual continuous-map ring of the finite normed extension. The theorem gives finite cohomological bounds for $N$ and $G$. Separately, lem-proper-heart-constructible-cohomology applies to these same two finite constant-model constructible sheaves and shows that $H^t(N)$ and $H^t(G)$ have finite constant models on finite constructible stratifications for every $t\geq0$. For $t<0$ both are zero. The equivalence def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence identifies internal modules with modules over the reconstructed ring sheaf. The latter category is Grothendieck by lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck, and hence has enough injectives by lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives. Apply lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative with $n=0$ to each degree-zero input to obtain a nonnegative injective complex, which that node also asserts is K-injective. Under the equivalence this remains a K-injective model. By sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, termwise module direct image of that model computes the actual unbounded derived direct image, and has zero terms in negative degrees. Hence $N\in\Dbc(S,A_E)$ and $G\in\Dbc(U,A_E)$ in the finite constant-model sense fixed in the statement. We use the first finiteness theorem only for bounds, not to replace finite constant models by local finite presentation.

source.place: Section 6.7 and Remark 6.8.15, printed p.62; precise continuous-coefficient bounds and finite constant-model cohomology are the two separately cited statements.

proof.text:
The open $W$ is nonempty (the alteration input gives $r$ surjective onto nonempty $S$), hence dense in the integral $Y$ and in $V$. The diagram $W\xrightarrow bV\xrightarrow{h_V}T^\circ$ is therefore a compactification of $s\circ r$ with $r$ proper. Apply det-sf-comp-composition-interchange(3) with its symbols $(\overline X,Y,\overline Y,W,p,i,j',r)$ replaced by $(W,S,T^\circ,V,r,s,b,h_V)$ and $A=L[0]$. The input belongs to $\Dctf$, hence to its localizing closure by definition. We obtain the normalized derived isomorphism $s_!N\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{V*}((b_!L)[0])$. Now $q=i\circ h_V$. The canonical internal-module compositor of lem-sfb-module-derived-compositor-coherence and exactness of closed direct image from det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf(2) give
$$G\simeq Ri_*Rh_{V*}((b_!L)[0])\simeq i_*s_!N.$$
By lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence, $i_*s_!$ is canonically the normalized $a_!$. Inverting the interchange comparison gives the required $G\simeq a_!N$. All comparisons are the cited canonical comparisons, with the open interchange normalized to the identity on $S$.

source.place: Clause (3), applied to W in V over the open S in T-circ; closed direct image and normalized locally closed coherence then carry it to U.

proof.text:
Apply lem-sfb-derived-open-square-restriction to $r:W\to S$ and the quasi-compact open $v:S_0\hookrightarrow S$, with derived input $L[0]$. Its comparison is
$$v^*N\simeq Rr_{0*}(L|_{W_0}[0]).$$
The square is Cartesian, and the coefficient identifications of sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients identify $L|_{W_0}$ with $r_0^*(M|_{S_0})$. This is the second required derived isomorphism. It uses only open base change, so no generic separability assumption is introduced.

source.place: Clause (2), derived restriction to an open, applied to S_0 in S.

proof.text: The image of the closed immersion $i:T^\circ\hookrightarrow U$ is the closure of $S$ in $U$: closure in an open subspace is the intersection with that open, and $T$ was the reduced closure in $X$. The isomorphism of step 6 writes $G$ as $i_*s_!N$. Its restriction to the complementary open is zero by det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf(2), termwise and hence in the derived category. This proves the stated support assertion. The constructions also cover rank zero, $D=\varnothing$, and $A_{\rm out}=\varnothing$; we have not replaced $D$ by $Y\setminus W_0$. Finally transport the coefficient actions back using step 1; all displayed isomorphisms and finite scalar models survive that identification.

The statement matches live; live is unsplit, svc.log shows no prior landing and there is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply and the delivery is not superseded. Step checks: (1) normed-coefficient-realization moves E isometrically into Q̄_ℓ, which the admissible-Λ and finite-subextension nodes require; relabelling along the ring isomorphism carries finite constant models, f*, b_! and i_*, and the 01T6 node gives Noetherianity. (2) T is integral and S connected; the hypotheses of potential-kummer-tameness (S nonempty, connected, separated, finite type) and of nested-open-regular-alteration (char p>0, T integral, S⊆T°⊆T dense opens, H nonempty connected finite étale surjective) all hold, and the outputs match the item's geometry, S₀/u/e/d≥1 and its disclaimers. (3) r, p, q are proper by the base-change, closed-immersion and composition nodes; p⁻¹U=V; L is lisse; tameness comes from the Kummer node with r factoring through H, and its parameter convention agrees with def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module. (4) L has the constant model A_E⊗E^n and Tor amplitude [0,0]; open-extension-finite-tor gives b_!L in Dctf and lfp form. (5) Bounds come from proper-dc-preserves-continuous; H^q for q≥0 has finite constant models by proper-heart (finite subextension, separated finite type); q<0 vanishes via a nonnegative K-injective model. (6) Interchange(3) with (W,S,T°,V,r,s,b,h_V): W is dense in integral V and L[0] lies in Loc(Dctf); the compositor, exact i_* (open-closed (2)) and locally-closed coherence (a=i∘u gives a_!≅i_*u_!) yield G≅a_!N. (7) Open-square restriction for the quasi-compact v gives v*N≅Rr₀*(r₀*(M|S₀)). (8) j*i_*=0 and the closure is T°. Edge cases checked: rank 0, D=∅, A_out=∅, inseparable degree, dim 0. Sources: ILO X Thm 2.1 and Lem 2.2 at printed pp.149-150, and Stacks 0F7B (torsion-only, so rightly not cited as a dependency). No SGA and no tags in the steps. Batch-5 flags: interchange and proper-heart reach lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison, a generic internal-module/ringed-topos equivalence, through proper base change, a six-functor input; the Kummer and nested-open nodes reach def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary, a general definition. None is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so all are accepted, and the tool_uses are accepted. Advisory: L[0]'s lfp constructibility (needed for step 5) is only implicit in step 4, but locally free of finite rank makes it elementary. No changes.
